steps.explanationAfterStep: A [3,3]-sigmatropic rearrangement: the σ bond moves from between atoms 3 and 4 to between atoms 1 and 6 (counted from each end), and both π bonds shift. The product is also a 1,5-diene, so the reaction can run backwards; here it goes forwards because the product's new alkene carries two carbon groups and is more stable than the starting terminal alkene. The six-membered transition state is chair-like with the methyl equatorial, so the new double bond is mainly E. The app does not check stereochemistry yet, so the drawings carry no wedges.

title: Cope rearrangement
subtitle: 3-Methylhexa-1,5-diene becomes hepta-1,5-diene by a [3,3] shift
references: Clayden, Greeves and Warren, Organic Chemistry, 2nd edition (Oxford University Press), chapter 35

diene.caption: 3-methylhexa-1,5-diene, drawn curled so its ends meet
hintTiers: Number the chain from one alkene end: 1=2–3–4–5=6. Which σ bond can break and which new σ bond can form, so that six electrons move round a six-membered ring?

The σ bond in the middle of the chain (between the carbon carrying the methyl and its CH₂ neighbour) breaks, a new σ bond forms between the two alkene ends, and both π bonds move one place inwards. Three arrows.

Arrow 1: from one C=C π bond to a new bond between the two CH₂ ends of the chain. Arrow 2: from the central σ bond to the bond between the methyl-bearing carbon and its alkene neighbour. Arrow 3: from the other C=C π bond to the bond between its CH and the CH₂ that lost the σ bond.
diene.learnerPrompt: On heating, a σ bond moves along the 1,5-diene. Draw the single step.

misconceptions.feedbackMessage: That σ bond is next to a C=C. In a [3,3] shift the bond that breaks is the central one, three atoms from each new bond end.
The methyl group stays put. The σ bond that moves is the C–C bond in the middle of the chain.

partialProgressMessages.feedbackMessage: Two of three. The CH₂ at the other end has made a new bond but still has its π bond: that π pair moves inwards to the carbon that lost the σ bond.

mechanismSummary: The Cope rearrangement is the [3,3]-sigmatropic shift of a hexa-1,5-diene: one σ bond and two π bonds reorganise through a chair-shaped six-membered transition state, with no intermediate. Because the product is another 1,5-diene, the reaction is an equilibrium, pulled towards the more substituted (more stable) alkenes. The chair transition state with substituents equatorial explains the E geometry of the new alkene. The app does not check stereochemistry yet, so the drawings carry no wedges.
